title: 50 Days of AI assisted game dev progression, I updated my demo today
author: ForkedPush
selftext:
I have 6 years of game design experience, and I recently started my AI-assisted game dev journey.

This is a cozy Fishing RPG I started developing with Opus 5.5 about a month and a half ago. I uploaded the demo to Steam two weeks ago, and today I pushed an update that fixes the issues you pointed out, plus some things I found in my own playtests.

As a solo dev, AI is a life changer. I’ve always had lots of cool game ideas, but time was the problem. I couldn’t sit down and work on a single game for years, because it wasn’t economically possible. Now I write a GDD, split it into tasks, and tell Claude what to do. It’s like my old office job, except I finally have the creative freedom my boss never gave me.

It’s still not easy. There are always bugs, and almost everything needs a manual touch. I do the level and game design 100% myself. I sometimes use free animations from Mixamo and similar places, and sometimes open-source tools for models. Claude’s main job is creating assets through the Blender MCP, like the vegitation, tools, some clothing the player is wearing etc. I found out that the AI produces the best result if you give them visual references, even a half assed doddle can help tremendously. It’s crazy that I could build this in under two months. The demo alone would have taken me at least a year.

I honestly don’t understand all the hate AI-assisted games get. I disclosed AI use on my Steam page because I think transparency matters. But after seeing the recent news on the hate AI games get I am having doubts on that decision, and I’d like to hear how other devs here handle it.

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5351000/I\_Just\_Wanted\_to\_Fish\_Demo/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5351000/I_Just_Wanted_to_Fish_Demo/)

replies.author: ForkedPush
replies.body:
Hey, thanks for the feedback and the kind words! I agree the fishing in the demo is limited. I kept it that way on purpose because I’m wary of people cloning ideas I’ve worked on, and the demo is only about 1/5 of what I’m building.

To answer your questions:

* You can’t upgrade fishing gear in the demo yet.
* The demo has two fishing styles: bobber fishing and deep fishing (set the depth to the lowest to use it).
* It already has different fish for different areas, depths and lures, and that will keep growing.

My GDD has plenty more fishing mechanics planned, and I hope they turn out well!

replies.author: Ok_Feedback4200
replies.body:
Hah, I wouldn't worry about people getting ur ideas.. personally i just try to make games 1) fun 2) realistic.. but fun takes priority.

So here's my wishlist for a fishing game...

1) shore fishing types: feeder, spinning, fly fishing.. this alone can go soooo deep if you look into different systems, baits and lures and have them craftable...
2) fishing from a boat - reaching big depths
3) underwater fishing - this is least important imo as it makes the underwater world the primary one..

But if keeping fishing from shore, i'd just want it to be realistic.. choosing the bait for the right fish, choosing the right location and place, etc.. then the fishing mechanics itself being different in still or moving water, your casted bait actually doing what its supposed to do when casted..

Fishing is a very deep hobby. So a fishing game can go very deep too...
